chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hadid, who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: When your skin shivers, your eyes shed tears, and your heart feels fear, then you are close (to God); you have achieved your goal.

key_terms.قصد: To aim for or achieve a goal
key_terms.وجل: To feel fear or anxiety (in a spiritual context)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical signs that indicate a prayer or supplication is accepted in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a diagnostic criterion for the acceptance of du'a, linking visceral physical reactions—such as skin trembling (iqshirar) and weeping—to the state of khushu' (humility) in the heart. This tradition reflects the Shia emphasis on the unity of body and spirit in worship, where external manifestations serve as reliable indicators of internal spiritual sincerity and divine proximity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-6 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Ali ibn Hadid who linked it up to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
If your body shakes, your tears flow and you fear (God) wholeheartedly, then you can be hopeful of God’s forgiveness, since you have achieved your goal.”
